# `useApi` response envelope is not unwrapped

- `useApi`'s `doFetch` (and the `useApiWithAuthZ`/`useApiWithTenantAuthZ` wrappers) returns the raw parsed JSON body. It never unwraps the backend's `{ status, message, data, meta, errors }` envelope.
- Type the `useApi<T>` / `useApiWithTenantAuthZ<T>` generic as the full envelope (e.g. `{ data: { fileName: string; text: string } }`), then read `.data` explicitly at the call site.
- **Why:** `T` is caller-supplied and unchecked against the real response shape. Typing it as the inner payload directly (skipping `data`) type-checks cleanly, but every field silently reads as `undefined` at runtime — no test or type-check catches the mismatch.

# Frontend Icons & Imports

## Icons

- Web (`frontend-admin`): import from `@phosphor-icons/react`.
- Mobile (`frontend-app`): import from `phosphor-react-native`.
- Import with `Icon` suffix (e.g. `FileTextIcon`).
- Always set `weight="thin"` on icons — Phosphor's own default is `regular`.

## Imports

- Within a package, use the `@/*` alias (frontend-admin, configured in `tsconfig.json`) or the shortest available relative path. Do not chain `../../..` more than two levels.
- Cross-package imports always go through the package name (e.g. `from 'up-types'`, `from 'up-design-tokens'`), never `../../up-types/src`.
- **Why:** deep relative chains and `/src` imports bypass the package's public `exports` boundary and break when the package is built or refactored.
- **Import `up-utils` via its subpath exports** (`up-utils/language`, `up-utils/runtime-env`, …), never the root `up-utils` barrel — the barrel pulls in Kafka/image node-heavy code that must not reach the browser bundle.

# Abstraction & Reuse

- Extract only what encodes non-obvious logic, an invariant, or a derived field; inline pass-through wrappers and single-use guards.
- Needed by 2+ packages → `up-types` (schema-adjacent data), `up-utils` (helpers with runtime deps), `up-api` (contracts, live layers).
- Never copy a body — delegate variants to the canonical implementation; parameterize near-duplicates.
- Backend is the source of truth — never round-trip server-derivable context through the client.
- Reuse by contract, not capability: call an existing function only if its intent fits, every required arg is meaningful (no faked values), all its side effects are wanted, and you're on its primary path — not an edge branch. Fail any one = don't call it; extend the primitive meant for your case (an additive optional field isn't "new abstraction") or write purpose-built code.
- A directive to reuse, or to avoid new tables/columns, is about persistence and the right component — not always mandate to call existing code to shrink the diff. Modifying a well-fitting primitive beats calling an ill-fitting one.

# Frontend Error Handling

## Both packages
- `useApi*` hooks already throw `ApiError`/`HttpError` (with `status`) and store `error` in their own state. Don't `try/catch` just to mirror that into local state — only catch when you act on failure.
- For HTTP 402: use `isCreditError(err)` (admin) or `Effect.tapErrorTag('up-api/PaymentRequiredError', ...)` (app). Never string-match `error.message`.
- Normalize `unknown` from `catch` with `error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error))`. Never `as Error`.
- `throw new Error` is reserved for context-misuse guards (`useX must be used within an XProvider`).

## frontend-admin
- User-facing errors: `useAlert().showAlert({ type: 'error', title, message? })` from `@/app/context/AlertContext`.

The guard isn't arbitrary — it falls out of a bigger architectural change this plan is making, and the "why" is worth separating from the bug the other agent found.

**What's changing:** Today, course creation is scattered — 7 different client call sites (`uploadContextFiles`, `attachFileSource`, `attachWebSourceUrl`, `refreshSources`, `fetchSourceText`, etc.) each lazily call `ensureDraftCourse()` if no course exists yet, so a draft `POST /courses` can fire from all over the place. The plan moves course/session creation entirely server-side: the *first* chat message (`POST /courses/creation-chat/message` with just `{ message }`) creates the draft course + session as a side effect, generates the title concurrently, and returns `courseUuid` in the `done` payload (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:978, 14). Line 982 states the goal explicitly: *"no client code path creates draft courses."*

**Why that motivates deleting `ensureDraftCourse` and guarding instead of replacing it:** Once course creation is centralized on the server's first-turn handler, the client has no sanctioned way to mint a `courseUuid` on its own anymore — there's no more `POST /courses` call available to these helper functions. `uploadContextFiles` and friends are all scoped to `/courses/{courseUuid}/context/...`, so they're inert without one. Rather than give each of the 7 call sites its own fallback course-creation logic (which would just resurrect the scattered-creation problem this refactor is trying to kill), the plan's premise (S1, line 139) was: *these functions are only ever reachable after the first turn has already happened*, because "the chat always starts with a first message" (line 16) — i.e., by the time a user could possibly attach/upload something, `courseUuid` is assumed to already be sitting in state. Under that assumption, hitting `courseUuid === null` in one of these functions isn't a real user path — it'd only happen from a stray/stale call (e.g., a race during `resetSession`), so early-returning is a cheap defensive no-op, not a UX gap.

So `courseUuid` is null precisely when a real user hits this path, not just in edge-case races, which is exactly why S1's blanket assumption doesn't hold and the guard silently eats the files instead of being the harmless no-op it was designed to be.

Effect-TS is the core paradigm on the backend and up-ai. It handles dependency injection, typed errors, structured concurrency, and distributed tracing in one model.

- Convert non-Effect code at boundaries with `Effect.tryPromise` / `Effect.try` — keep Promise/throw-style code limited to boundary adapters.

- Declare dependencies by yielding them inside `Effect.gen` — always yield them from context.
- Wrap every public method with `Effect.withSpan('ServiceName.methodName')` for free OpenTelemetry tracing.
- Export a composed `XxxLive` layer that wires all sub-dependencies. The entry point provides these layers to the running program.
- Use `Effect.fn` for functions that return Effects — gives automatic tracing.

## Domain Types
- Domain IDs are branded (`CourseUuid`, `LevelUuid`, …) via `Schema.brand()` in `up-types` — the compiler prevents passing the wrong ID type. Use the branded type; never widen to a plain `string`.
- Define new shared types with Effect `Schema` for runtime validation plus inferred TypeScript types.

## Tests
- Use `new ServiceClass({...})` to create typed mock instances for `Layer.succeed` in tests. This only works for `Effect.Service` classes, not `Context.Tag`.

That resolves the open question, and it also overturns the "send-first, deferred upload, follow-up turn" design I proposed a few messages ago — that design is wrong given what you just described, and I should say so plainly rather than patch around it.

**Why it's wrong:** the digest list is built fresh into *every* turn's system prompt from `GET /courses/:id/context/digests` — it's not something that arrives later via a special follow-up message. If turn 1 fires before the upload+digest step completes, turn 1's system prompt has no "Attached sources" entry at all, the model can't `gather_context` against something it doesn't know exists, and citation numbering (`byAttachmentOrder`) hasn't even been established yet. A second, materials-aware turn afterward is not "the same pipeline" — it's a materially different (and worse) one. So: upload and digest-processing must complete **before** the first turn's LLM call, not after it.

**Which means the actual conflict is with S1 itself, not with frontend call ordering.** Under S1, `courseUuid` only exists after the first turn's response is *successfully delivered* — but uploading a file requires a `courseUuid` to attach it to, and that upload+digest must finish *before* the first turn's LLM call runs whenever there's a staged file. 2. User sends the first message → *now*, before the turn's LLM call: ensure the course exists (create it if needed — this is the one legitimate pre-turn creation trigger) → upload the staged file(s) against it → wait for digest processing to complete.
3. Only then does the first turn actually run — its system prompt already has the "Attached sources" digest list, exactly like any regular turn with sources attached, exactly like `gather_context` already works today.

# Implementation Plan — Course-Creation Chat Backend Persistence

Source of truth: `course-creation/chat-persistence-design.md` (design locked). This plan turns that design into three stand-alone, independently testable phases. Each phase compiles, passes `pnpm type-check` and `pnpm test`, and contains no stubs or placeholder implementations.

## 1. What the feature does

The course-creation chat currently keeps all conversation state in the browser: every turn the client re-sends the full `history`, `briefPin`, `artifact`, `lastOutline`, and `sources`, and the backend rebuilds an in-memory session, streams the answer, and persists nothing. Closing the browser loses the conversation.

After this plan:

- **Chats persist server-side.** Two new tables (`chat_sessions`, `chat_turns`) store the transcript, the latest artifact/brief/outline, and per-turn on-change snapshots. The client sends only `{ courseUuid?, message }`.
- **Chats are resumable from `/courses`.** The grid includes draft courses; a draft card shows "Draft" and clicking it reopens the chat at `/get-started?course=<uuid>` with the full transcript, artifact, brief, outline, and sources restored via `GET /courses/:courseUuid/chat-session`.
- **Finalized courses are re-editable through the chat** ("Edit with AI" from masterbrain). On open, the artifact is rebuilt from the live `courses_levels` rows (the course is the source of truth); within an open chat each turn builds on the session's artifact, so multi-turn edits accumulate until re-finalize (S12), which performs a content-aware sync by `levelUuid` instead of appending duplicate levels.
- The first turn creates the draft course server-side, generates a course title with a small model concurrently, and returns the `courseUuid` the client uses from then on.

Stays on the frontend (transient UI only): composer text, open/closed panels, drag-hover, streaming buffers. The chat always starts with a first message, so a `courseUuid` exists before any source upload; all client-side draft creation is removed.
